tracks.title: 酸菜罈子蓋
tracks.subject: a young man carries his own three-year-old jar of pickled mustard greens to his girlfriend's flat to cook for her, and the lid will not open for him, her roommate or her brother, until she taps it once with a spoon handle

tracks.title: 舊書店的鉛筆字
tracks.subject: the owner of a tiny second-hand bookshop writes each price in pencil on the inside cover, and one Saturday buys back a novel from a woman who sold it to him last spring, finding a pressed ticket stub in it that is now his to keep or return

tracks.title: 公園裡的小板凳
tracks.genre: Mandarin Irish folk session (fiddle and tin whistle)
tracks.subject: a matchmaking auntie in a city park carries forty paper resumes, notices two of her clients, a bus mechanic and a pharmacist, both walk the same path at six every morning, and quietly moves her folding stool until they have to sit beside each other

tracks.title: 送報的檸檬
tracks.subject: a woman who delivers newspapers by bicycle before dawn down one Tainan lane folds each paper differently for a retired teacher, who hangs one lemon on the gatepost every Friday, and she has been counting the lemons

tracks.title: 論文要訂好
tracks.subject: a bookbinder is handed a hundred-page doctoral thesis at midnight that must be bound and on a desk by nine, and he cannot stop reading the dedication page, which names the student's cleaning-lady mother

tracks.title: 最後一球灰藍線
tracks.subject: two strangers reach on a Saturday for the very last ball of grey-blue wool of the same dye lot in a Beipu wool shop; the shop auntie winds it into two balls so they each knit half, and the two scarves match

tracks.title: 卡帶轉啊轉
tracks.subject: a long-haul truck driver on the Sichuan-Tibet highway whose only cassette was chewed by the deck, winds it back with a pencil at every rest stop, and now the song wobbles and he sings along with the wobble

tracks.title: 我的底片有你的手指
tracks.subject: a young man develops the roll from the old film camera his girlfriend borrowed on a Hualien coast trip and finds that all twenty-four frames have the tip of her thumb in the corner, and he asks the lab to print them all

tracks.title: 京胡的音準
tracks.subject: a piano tuner called to an opera troupe's practice room finds the upright piano tuned to A 440 while the jinghu player insists on a lower pitch, so the two argue and finally meet in the middle

tracks.title: 四十七號掛在我手裡
tracks.subject: a cloakroom girl at a Shanghai-style hotel ballroom keeps hanging the same man's coat on hook number 47, because he keeps losing his ticket on purpose to stay and chat

tracks.title: 兩個名字刻一顆
tracks.genre: Inner Mongolian long-song (urtiin duu) style ballad with tovshuur and limbe
tracks.subject: a stone name-seal carver in a lane workshop whose young couple customers cannot agree on a name for their baby, so he carves one name on each end of the same stone and tells them to press both

tracks.title: 三分鐘的側臉
tracks.subject: a street paper-cutting artist who cuts silhouette portraits in three minutes, and the man who cannot stop smiling while he sits still, so the paper face comes out grinning and she keeps it

tracks.title: 車掌今天不重複
tracks.subject: a city bus conductor with a punch pliers who calls every stop in a brand-new rhyme and never repeats one, while the regulars secretly keep a tally to bet he cannot last a whole day

tracks.title: 三年前的那只鐘
tracks.genre: Quebec chanson with accordion and upright bass (Mandarin storytelling)
tracks.subject: a clock repairer whose window is lined with fixed clocks nobody collected, and the woman who comes to pick hers up three years late and is told she is only three years behind

tracks.title: 白手套的路口
tracks.genre: Levantine dabke folk-pop with mijwiz, oud and tabla
tracks.subject: a traffic officer in white gloves at a busy crossroads whose hand signals start to follow a stomping beat, until pedestrians, delivery riders and a bus driver fall into step and the whole crossing moves in a line

tracks.title: 掌紋接上了
tracks.subject: a young woman who reads palms at a night-market folding table, a trade her grandfather taught her, and the man who sits down, asks no question about money or exams, and whose palm lines meet hers exactly when they touch

tracks.title: 磨到剩一片柳葉
tracks.subject: a hotel kitchen apprentice who inherits the retired chef's thirty-year-old cleaver, worn narrow as a willow leaf, resists changing its shape on the whetstone, and finds the handle already dented to fit his thumb

tracks.title: 黃旗搖搖過馬路
tracks.subject: a retired volunteer crossing guard at a Tainan primary-school corner waving his big yellow flag at 7:20 each morning, and the day he is five minutes late and the children stop the traffic with his flag themselves

tracks.title: 水桶裡找洞
tracks.subject: a bicycle-shop mender who dunks inner tubes in a water bucket to find the leak by its bubbles, and the young man who comes back every afternoon at 4:30 with a tyre that has no puncture at all, on a bike he rents by the hour just to stand by her bucket

tracks.title: 多撥一顆珠
tracks.subject: a stationery-shop abacus teacher in her sixties whose Saturday class gets one retired vegetable seller, who gets every sum wrong by exactly one bead so that she has to lean over to fix it, and the day he finally gets one right

tracks.title: 陳怡君請上車
tracks.subject: Number 17 of forty-three women all named 陳怡君 on their namesake club's coach trip, where roll call is one name answered forty-three times; when a rest-area loudspeaker pages the late one, three strangers with that name come running too.

tracks.title: 老樣子
tracks.subject: A woman who studies her hand-shaken tea shop's sixty-item menu board for five minutes every evening while the queue sighs, then orders the same light-sugar, no-ice Four Seasons oolong as always, until the clerk laminates a one-item menu just for her.

tracks.title: 我姓范姜
tracks.subject: A Taoyuan man with the rare double surname 范姜 has been called 'Mr. Fan' all his life by teachers, waiters and couriers, until the one courier who reads his parcel label right turns out to be a 張簡, forever 'Mr. Zhang'.

tracks.title: 你坐我右邊
tracks.subject: A left-handed woman and right-handed boyfriend whose elbows knocked all through their first date at a seven-stool ramen counter; now she always sits on his left so they can eat and hold hands, and when only the wrong seats are free, both eat wrong-handed.

tracks.title: 站上牛奶箱
tracks.mood: tender, warm, quietly proud, gently buoyant
tracks.subject: Best friends since first grade, one 191 cm and always back-row centre, one 158 cm and always front-row centre in every class photo, open a café together; for the opening-day picture the short one stands on a milk crate so their heads are level.

tracks.title: 冷凍庫裝不下
tracks.subject: a woman who meal-preps twenty-one lunch boxes every Sunday night and plays Tetris to fit them into the tiny freezer of her shared flat, evicting her flatmate's ice cream tub one box at a time

tracks.title: 一刀不斷
tracks.subject: an office worker whose secret hobby is peeling an apple in one unbroken strip, practising every night on supermarket apples to beat his own record of two point three metres while his girlfriend is made to eat every apple

tracks.title: 記帳本
tracks.subject: a couple who share one paper spending notebook on the kitchen table, where she writes small remarks beside his entries like 'braised snacks 85, didn't share', until he realises the ledger has become their diary

tracks.title: 櫥窗第三格
tracks.subject: a young woman who walks past a shoe shop every evening to look at one pair of red leather heels in the third window slot priced 4,280, saving 150 dollars a day in a tin and counting how many days are left before someone else buys them

tracks.title: 咖哩第七天
tracks.genre: Mandarin New Orleans second-line brass pop
tracks.subject: a man who misreads grams in a curry recipe, cooks a five-kilo pot, and has to eat it for seven days, reinventing it each night as curry udon, curry toast, curry fried rice and curry hotpot
